panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Panel A shows the classic scimitar vein draining to the inferior vena cava on angiography, a defining manifestation of scimitar syndrome. B: Panel B shows angiography of an upper pulmonary vein draining directly into the superior vena cava, an unusual variant in this scimitar syndrome case; no exact vocabulary finding matches. C: Panel C shows a middle pulmonary vein draining into the azygos vein and then the superior vena cava, part of the unusual scimitar syndrome anatomy described in this case. D: Panel D is a lateral angiographic view confirming the anomalous middle pulmonary vein drainage into the azygos vein and superior vena cava.

in_text_mentions: Cardiac catheterization was performed preoperatively to clarify the anatomy for exact planning of the operative strategy (Figure 2). The angiography demonstrated an anomalous drainage from the right lower lobe to the inferior vena cava (as shown in MRI), from the right upper lobe to the superior vena cava and middle pulmonary vein connected to the azygos vein. There were no systemic-to-pulmonary collateral arteries and an overall left-to-right shunt of 40% with normal pulmonary artery pressure.
